label: Camera grammar — physical phrasing for generative video
source: pgc-skills-export/us-pre/longpoll-consistant references/seedance2-prompts.md (constant-motion wording, non-final ending) + references/continuity-spec.md (failure matrix); us-pre/generate-camera-blocking-board references/board-spec.md (one dominant movement per panel); us-pre/video-storyboard (panel variety)
why: Generative video models read 'slow' and 'cinematic' as style, not velocity, and their implied speed changes between generations. Every move below is phrased as observable physics — what changes in frame, and at what rate — so two shots asking for the same move actually get the same move.

static.phrase: the camera is locked on a tripod and does not move; framing, height, and focal length stay fixed for the whole shot

dolly-in.phrase: the camera travels forward at a constant slow walking pace, subject distance decreasing steadily, focal length unchanged, floor parallax continuous

dolly-out.phrase: the camera travels backward at a constant slow walking pace, subject distance increasing steadily, focal length unchanged, more of the set entering frame

truck-left.phrase: the camera slides laterally to screen left at a constant rate while holding its heading, foreground objects sweeping right-to-left faster than the background

truck-right.phrase: the camera slides laterally to screen right at a constant rate while holding its heading, foreground objects sweeping left-to-right faster than the background

pan-left.phrase: the camera stays in place and rotates on its vertical axis toward screen left at a constant angular rate, no lateral translation, no parallax shift between foreground and background

pan-right.phrase: the camera stays in place and rotates on its vertical axis toward screen right at a constant angular rate, no lateral translation, no parallax shift between foreground and background

tilt-up.phrase: the camera stays in place and pitches upward at a constant angular rate, the horizon dropping steadily through frame

tilt-down.phrase: the camera stays in place and pitches downward at a constant angular rate, the horizon rising steadily through frame

crane-up.phrase: the camera rises vertically at a constant rate while holding its heading, lens height increasing, the ground plane opening up below

crane-down.phrase: the camera descends vertically at a constant rate while holding its heading, lens height decreasing toward the subject

orbit.phrase: the camera arcs around the subject at a constant radius and constant angular rate, subject distance unchanged, the background sweeping continuously behind them

handheld-follow.phrase: a handheld camera follows the subject from a constant distance and height, with small continuous irregular sway and natural step-induced bounce, never losing the subject from frame

steadicam-follow.phrase: a stabilized camera follows the subject at a constant distance and constant height, floating without step bounce, the subject holding the same screen position throughout

whip-pan.phrase: the camera rotates rapidly on its vertical axis, producing directional motion blur across the whole frame, starting and ending on a readable composition

rack-focus.phrase: the camera does not move; focus shifts from the foreground plane to the background plane at a steady rate, depth of field unchanged

zoom-in.phrase: the camera body stays in place while focal length increases at a steady rate, perspective compressing, no parallax change

clauses.oneDominantMove: Use exactly one dominant camera movement for the whole shot. Do not combine a pan with a dolly, or add a second move partway through.
clauses.noEditing: This is a single continuous take from one physical camera. Do not cut, switch viewpoint, teleport the camera, insert reaction coverage, or create montage.
clauses.noEaseOut: The shot ends during uninterrupted motion: the camera holds its declared speed and direction through the final frame. Do not decelerate, settle, hold, or form an ending composition.
clauses.alreadyMoving: At frame zero the camera is already moving at the declared speed. Do not start from rest and do not add a new-shot ease-in.
